home.title: Your health information, one tap away when it matters.
home.text: Save your allergies, medications and emergency contacts. When the NFC tag or QR code on your bracelet or tag is scanned, the person helping sees only what you chose to share, with no app to install.

privacy.title: Privacy and usage notice
privacy.draft: This text is a draft notice prepared as part of the application's development. It is not a guarantee of legal compliance and should be reviewed by a legal professional before launch.

sections.title: Data controller
body: This application was built as a software engineering course project. Before launch, the data controller's name and contact details (for example an email address) must be added here: [NAME / ORGANISATION – CONTACT EMAIL].

sections.title: What data do we collect?
body: Account details: full name, email address and a one-way hash of your password (the password itself is never stored).
Health profile: date of birth, blood type, allergies, chronic conditions, regular medications and an emergency note. You enter these yourself and all of them are optional.
Emergency contacts: name, relationship and phone number. Please inform anyone before adding their details.
Access records: when and how (link/NFC/QR or short code) your emergency page was opened, plus a truncated IP address. No precise location or device identifier is collected.
Session cookie: a cookie required to keep you logged in. No advertising or tracking cookies are used.

sections.title: Why do we process it, and on what basis?
body: Account details are processed to create your account and let you log in.

Health data is special-category personal data. It is processed only to show it to people who help you in an emergency, based on the explicit consent you give separately at registration. This consent is separate from other consents and you can withdraw it by deleting your account.
Access records are kept to show you when your page was opened and to help you notice misuse.

sections.title: How does the emergency page work?
body: Only a personal, very hard-to-guess link is written to your tag or QR code. Health information is never written to the tag.
Anyone who knows this link can open your page without logging in. The page shows only the details you chose to show; hidden fields are never sent by the server.
Do not share the link publicly. If you lose your tag, revoke the link from the dashboard; the old link will show nothing and you can create a new one.
The page is marked so that search engines do not index it, but the real protection is the unguessable link and the limited data shown.

sections.title: Why are contact details shown?
body: The name, relationship and phone number of your emergency contacts are shown so that the person helping you can reach them quickly on your behalf. You can turn this off at any time.

sections.title: How do we protect your data?
body: Health data is stored encrypted field by field. Passwords are hashed with Argon2id. Links and short codes are generated randomly and only their digests are stored. In production only HTTPS is used.
No system is risk-free, so we recommend entering only information you really want to share.

sections.title: How long do we keep it, and how can you delete it?
body: Access records are kept for at most 30 days and then deleted automatically.

From account settings you can at any time (1) delete only your health data and access history, or (2) delete your account completely. When an account is deleted, your profile, links, short codes and all related data are deleted and can no longer be accessed.
This project keeps no separate records that are legally required to be retained; this should be re-evaluated before launch.

sections.title: Your rights
body: Under Article 11 of Turkish Personal Data Protection Law No. 6698 you have the right to learn whether your data is processed, request information, request correction or deletion, and object to processing. You can correct and delete data yourself from the dashboard; for other requests use the contact details above.

sections.title: About use
body: This application shows information that users enter themselves in an emergency. It is not a verified medical record; the user is responsible for its accuracy and currency.
In a medical emergency, call 112 first. This application is not a medical device and does not replace professional healthcare.
Keep your information up to date, revoke the link if you lose your tag, and do not add someone else's information without their knowledge.

tags.nfcTitle: How to write it to an NFC tag
nfcSteps: Get an NFC tag such as NTAG213, NTAG215 or NTAG216. All three can hold this link.
Install an app such as NFC Tools on your phone.
In the app, go to Write, choose Add a record and select the URL/URI type.
Paste the link above and tap OK.
Tap Write, then hold the phone against the tag until it confirms.
Test the tag and check that your page opens in the phone's browser.
tags.nfcNote: Only this link should be written to the tag. Do not lock the tag; if you renew the link you will need to rewrite it.
